system.name: ST-TTC
system.one_liner: Test-time computing paradigm for spatio-temporal forecasting: a lightweight spectral-domain calibrator corrects predictions in real time, updated by a flash mechanism with a streaming memory queue.

content.variant_note: three sibling formula chains (a) to (c) in one grammar, the proposed one given the wide bottom row
content.argues: Unlike test-time training and online continual learning, which optimise the whole model or internal parameters, test-time computing optimises only a small calibrator g after the forecaster.
content.subject: Three formula chains (input, model, output, loss) with the parameters optimised at test time marked in red.

evidence: Conceptual visualization comparison of different spatio-temporal learning paradigms under test environment.
Our (c) Test-Time Computing method only requires a lightweight calibrator gθ, which is a seamless and lightweight plug-and-play module.
Red represents the parameters that need to be optimized during the test.

summary: ST-TTC is a test-time computing paradigm for spatio-temporal forecasting that adds a lightweight spectral-domain calibrator after the forecaster and updates it with a flash mechanism. Figure 1 compares three learning paradigms under test conditions as three chains of grey equation boxes in the same grammar: (a) Test-Time Training, where the model f_θ is trained through a pretext loss on x; (b) Online Continual Learning, where internal parameters θ(δ) are optimised against the target y; and (c) Test-Time Computing, where the forecaster stays unchanged and only the calibrator g_θ, marked in red, sits before the loss. A key sentence explains the red, and dotted rules separate the panels.
summary_zh: ST-TTC 是时空预测的测试时计算范式。图 1 用三条同样语法的公式框链并列比较：(a) 测试时训练、(b) 在线持续学习、(c) 测试时计算；红色符号标出测试时要优化的参数，(c) 只优化校准器 g。
notes: The pre-screen listed side-by-side-contrast only; concept-schematic is added because the figure is a formal chain of boxed equations. The role of the tilde on x in (a) as a modified input is read from the caption's pretext-task wording. The figure has no pictures, icons or examples.
